blocks.text: Rank summaries used 5,000 common patient-cluster bootstrap samples of the fixed external predictions (102 hospitalization episodes from 50 patients; 67 event episodes). In each sample, 50 patients were drawn with replacement, retaining all eligible episodes and their sampling multiplicities; performance remained episode-weighted. Models were ranked separately by higher AUROC, higher AP and lower Brier score, with rank 1 denoting the best value. Tied positions were equally apportioned using a numerical tolerance of 10⁻¹². Mean rank was averaged across samples; first-place and top-three shares sum the corresponding apportioned rank frequencies. All 5,000 samples were valid for each metric. Shares are descriptive resampling summaries, not probabilities that a model is truly optimal.

blocks.text: Point differences were calculated in the complete external cohort. Paired 95% percentile bootstrap CIs are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of within-sample differences from the same 5,000 patient-cluster samples used in panel E. Differences are RBF-SVM minus comparator for AUROC and AP, and comparator minus RBF-SVM for Brier; positive values favor RBF-SVM. SVM-leading frequency is the proportion of valid samples with a difference greater than 10⁻¹², with ties retained in the denominator; it is not a P value. All 5,000 samples were valid for each comparison. The CIs are comparison-specific and unadjusted for multiplicity. Additional digits are retained for near-zero interval limits. Panels E and F summarize fixed predictions in the same external cohort: models were not refitted, and this exploratory analysis does not provide independent validation or adjust for model selection.
blocks.display_html: Point differences were calculated in the complete external cohort. Paired 95% percentile bootstrap CIs are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of within-sample differences from the same 5,000 patient-cluster samples used in panel E. All 5,000 samples were valid for each comparison. The CIs are comparison-specific and unadjusted for multiplicity. Additional digits are retained for near-zero interval limits.
